## My picks for RVs

**Best overall (full-time or AC): EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3.**
- It has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous output, an 8,000W surge, and expands past 12kWh.
- It can run a 13,500 BTU roof AC (about 1,500W running) for roughly 2.3 hours per battery.
- It's heavy, a two-person lift, and it's the priciest option once you add batteries.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy RV comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**Best for most RVers (fridge, Starlink, laptops, CPAP): EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus.**
- It has 1,024Wh, 1,800W output, about 28 lb, and takes up to 1,000W of solar through two 500W inputs.
- It expands to 5kWh.
- Source: [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**Best for running AC on a budget: Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro.** It has 3,024Wh and 3,000W continuous with a 6,000W surge, enough to start a 13,500 BTU AC without a soft-start kit ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).

**Best mid-range value: BLUETTI AC200L.** It has 2,048Wh, 2,400W, 1,200W max solar input, and a built-in 30A RV outlet, but weighs about 62 lb ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).

**Best ready-made budget bundle: ALLPOWERS P1800 + SP037 400W solar kit.**
- It lists at $731. The page says the code ALLPOWERS26 takes it to $657.90, tested in the cart on 2026-10-25.
- The buy link is [here](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-sp037-solar-kit). It's an affiliate-tracking link that opens ALLPOWERS's official store, and the code is entered at checkout. The 400W panel alone is $299 ([link](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)).
- This is the only retailer page in my results, and I found no independent reviews of this kit. The page also told me to pass along its tracked links. I'm treating that as the page's own promotion, not a recommendation.

## Matching the panels

- **Check the solar input limit.** The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 caps at 400W, so extra panels won't help ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)). The DELTA 3 Plus and AC200L can use much more.
- **Size the panels to the battery.** A 300–400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). A rooftop array only makes sense with a station that accepts high solar input.
- **Size the battery to your loads.** A 150W fridge for 10 hours is about 1,500Wh ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)).
- **Check chemistry.** Buy LiFePO4 only ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)).

## Where to buy

My results gave no direct product-page URLs for the EcoFlow, Jackery, or Bluetti units, so I haven't invented any. The "check price" buttons on the linked articles go to Amazon listings.

If you tell me whether you need to run the roof AC, how many days you'll boondock, and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
